title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten verified no-purchase outings on Georgia Tech’s campus and around Atlanta, spanning gardens, galleries, public art, transit, and museums.

cards.entity_name: Robert C. Williams Museum of Papermaking
cards.title: Trace Paper From Pulp to Press
cards.subtitle: Take a free self-guided museum visit beside campus
cards.notes: Bring a friend to compare historic tools, watermarks, industrial equipment, and the changing gallery before choosing a favorite object.
cards.short_summary: A weekday museum session built around paper history, technology, and changing exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum’s official visitor page states that self-guided visits are free to the public during museum hours and identifies its Georgia Tech location.
cards.source_title: Visit | Robert C. Williams Museum of Papermaking
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m. ET, except Georgia Tech holidays; self-guided public visits are free.

cards.entity_name: The Kendeda Building for Innovative Sustainable Design
cards.title: Decode a Living Building
cards.subtitle: Follow the public displays on a self-guided sustainability visit
cards.notes: Start in the atrium, follow the interpretive signs, then compare the rainwater, energy, and salvaged-material features with a friend.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced look at how a certified living building handles energy, water, and materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech states that the Kendeda Building is open to the public and offers self-guided visits using displays and informational signage, with no admission or purchase requirement listed.
cards.access_notes: Public self-guided visits are available during posted building hours; check the page for semester schedules and Institute-holiday closures.

cards.title: Work a Garden Plot Together
cards.subtitle: Volunteer in the campus growing space near the Instructional Center
cards.notes: Check the volunteer link before arriving, wear clothes suited to soil, and join planting, weeding, or harvesting work assigned that day.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on social session centered on food growing and practical garden care.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech identifies the Community Garden as a growing space open to all students, faculty, staff, and visitors and directs prospective volunteers to the campus sustainability organization.
cards.access_notes: Open access does not guarantee a staffed volunteer session; follow the official volunteer link and confirm the current meeting details first.

cards.title: Make Something by Hand
cards.subtitle: Join a free Georgia Tech Library art workshop
cards.notes: Check the upcoming-session link, invite a classmate, and arrive ready to try a listed activity such as origami or bookbinding.
cards.short_summary: A recurring hands-on library program connecting paper craft, art, and low-pressure conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library describes Tech’s Tactile Thursdays as artistic workshops and programming, including origami and bookbinding, that are free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: Attend only a currently listed session; dates, locations, capacity, and any registration instructions vary by workshop.

cards.title: Build a Campus Art Loop
cards.subtitle: Find named works across the Georgia Tech campus
cards.notes: Open the official collection and campus map, pick five named works, then trade interpretations and photos at each stop.
cards.short_summary: A customizable walking hang linking sculptures, murals, memorials, and campus history.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Arts invites visitors to view its campus public-art collection in person and directs them to the Arts layer on the campus map; the works are presented as public art rather than ticketed attractions.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor works can be viewed without admission; observe posted building-access rules before attempting to see indoor pieces.

cards.title: Ride the Stinger and Explore
cards.subtitle: Turn Georgia Tech’s free transit network into a campus loop
cards.notes: Choose two unfamiliar campus stops, ride together, and spend a few minutes exploring each area before boarding the return route.
cards.short_summary: A fare-free way to connect distant campus areas while planning a small shared outing.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech’s official visitor information states that a variety of free transit options operate around campus and to nearby destinations.
cards.access_notes: Check the live route information before leaving; service patterns and operating periods vary, and visitor parking is not free.

cards.title: Walk the EcoCommons Landscape
cards.subtitle: Follow paths through Georgia Tech’s campus greenspace network
cards.notes: Meet by the Kendeda side, follow the public paths, pause at the granite outcrop, and compare the landscape’s habitats and sensors.
cards.short_summary: A conversation-friendly walk through a designed landscape focused on biodiversity and stormwater.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech describes the EcoCommons as campus greenspace with walking paths, picnic and study areas, hammocks, tables, slides, and other freely usable outdoor features.
cards.source_title: EcoCommons | Georgia Tech Infrastructure and Operations
cards.access_notes: Stay on public paths and casual-use areas; designated lawns, platforms, and plazas may require reservations for organized use.

cards.title: Compare Notes in the Galleries
cards.subtitle: See contemporary exhibitions near Georgia Tech without paying admission
cards.notes: Register as requested, walk the galleries at your own pace, and each choose one work to discuss before leaving the campus.
cards.short_summary: A nearby contemporary-art outing with rotating exhibitions and no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Atlanta Contemporary’s official visitor page says admission is always free and asks visitors to register before arrival or at the door.
cards.access_notes: Registration is requested; confirm current exhibitions, opening hours, and installation closures on the official site before visiting.

cards.title: Follow Money Through the Fed
cards.subtitle: Take a free self-guided museum tour in Midtown
cards.notes: Go with a classmate, trace the exhibits on money and banking, and compare what surprised you before heading back to campus.
cards.short_summary: A weekday outing that turns monetary history and Federal Reserve operations into conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta states that its Monetary Museum is entirely free and that groups of fewer than ten may take self-guided weekday tours without scheduling.
cards.source_title: Atlanta Monetary Museum | Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta
cards.access_notes: Self-guided visits run Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m. ET, except federal holidays; review security and identification rules first.

cards.title: Walk an Open-Air Art Exhibit
cards.subtitle: Explore free murals and sculptures along the Atlanta Beltline
cards.notes: Choose a manageable trail segment, use the official art information to locate works, and pause for one group photo along the route.
cards.short_summary: A flexible outdoor art walk combining conversation, movement, and changing installations.
cards.evidence_claim: Atlanta Beltline’s official visitor page identifies Art on the Atlanta Beltline as a free public-art exhibition.
cards.access_notes: The exhibition requires no admission; select a daylight route, check trail alerts, and budget separately for optional transportation.
